answer:
## Headline (as-delivered file first, artifact named in the same breath)

**In the delivered NLSY79 1989 file (n=12,686, P(DISSAVED=1)=23.6%) dissaving declines weakly with age — adjusted OR 0.955/yr (0.938–0.973, p=6.5e-07), predicted P falling 0.253→0.185 from age 24→32 (−6.8 pp) — but that gradient is not robust: it is concentrated entirely in the curator's mean-imputed rows and disappears completely once they are excluded (OR 1.000, 0.979–1.021, p=0.91).** Curvature is marginal and not a U-shape: AGE_c²=−0.0089 (p=0.042), LR vs linear χ²=4.76, df=1, p=0.029, saturated age dummies add nothing (χ²=7.52, df=6, p=0.275), and the turning point (25.5) has a bootstrap CI of 18.6–26.8 that sits *mostly below* the 24–32 support. In the clean subset the quadratic dies (AGE_c²=−0.0029, p=0.56; joint-age LR p=0.84).

## Models (AGE_c = AGE−28)
| sample | model | AGE_c (p) | AGE_c² (p) | OR/yr | joint-age LR p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| as-delivered | age+age² | −0.0468 (0.000) | −0.0094 (0.030) | 0.954 | – |
| as-delivered | + GENDER,BLACK,HISPANIC,log(1+INC),INC0 | −0.0503 (0.000) | −0.0089 (0.042) | 0.951 | 0.000 |
| clean (n=8,430) | age+age² | +0.0137 (0.207) | −0.0035 (0.475) | 1.014 | – |
| clean | + same covariates | **−0.0012 (0.910)** | −0.0029 (0.560) | 0.999 | **0.844** |
| dedup (n=10,535) | + covariates | +0.0055 (0.579) | −0.0038 (0.394) | 1.006 | – |

Income-quartile robustness (no winsorizing) agrees: as-delivered AGE_c=−0.0386/AGE_c²=−0.0050; clean −0.0023/−0.0021.

## Age-specific AMEs (delta-method 95% CI) — the effect is small and shrinks to nothing
| age | AME full | 95% CI | pred P | AME clean | 95% CI | pred P |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|24|+0.0039|−0.0085,+0.0162|0.2532|+0.0045|−0.0108,+0.0197|0.2887|
|28|−0.0092|−0.0127,−0.0057|0.2422|−0.0003|−0.0047,+0.0042|0.2972|
|32|−0.0182|−0.0280,−0.0084|0.1851|−0.0049|−0.0219,+0.0120|0.2868|

## Mechanism: the gradient lives in the imputed rows (your ruling #3 test)
- Fill share by age: 0.287/0.289/0.262/0.260/0.325/0.382/0.411/0.404/**0.467** for ages 24→32. Fill share by outcome: **0.387 among DISSAVED=0 vs 0.170 among DISSAVED=1**.
- was_imputed model: OR=0.272 (p<1e-16), AME=−0.273; age terms shrink to AGE_c=−0.0327 (p=0.0009), AGE_c²=−0.0052 (p=0.246).
- Interaction *inside* the full sample (correct test — the clean subset overlaps the full one, so an independent-samples Wald would be invalid): linear age×fill χ²=38.65, df=1, p=5e-10; quadratic interaction χ²=39.64, df=2. Age slope among non-filled rows **−0.0004 (p=0.97)**, additional slope inside filled rows **−0.1513 (p<1e-10)**; stratum fits: filled-only OR/yr 0.872 (0.837–0.908, p=3e-11) vs clean-only 1.015 (0.994–1.036, p=0.16).
- Duplicates are the fill artifact, as you predicted: 2,151 exact duplicates are almost all mean-fill signatures, and dropping only them kills the gradient (p=0.58).

## Two substantive readings beyond the artifact
1. **Composition, not withdrawing, moves with age.** Multinomial (base = same/no savings): as-delivered "saved more vs same" AGE=+0.1119 (p<1e-16) while "dissave vs same" is null (+0.0095, p=0.39); clean subset both null (p=0.97, p=0.61). The "saved more" share grows 31.5%→49.5% by age group in the delivered file but only 26.8%→31.1% in clean data. So the pooled DISSAVED=0 category, not dissaving itself, generates the ordering.
2. **Income dominates.** Clean adjusted log(1+INCOME) OR=1.365 per log-dollar (1.295–1.440, p<1e-29), AME 0.063/log-unit; p10→p90 income shifts predicted P by **+0.123** vs **−0.002** for the whole 24→32 age span. Raw quintile rates 17.3/29.0/32.8/34.2/35.3%. As-delivered income coefficient is itself attenuated to OR 1.111 because 31% of rows sit exactly on the fill value. Others: Black OR 1.36 (p<1e-7), male 0.91 (p=0.04), Hispanic 1.07 (p=0.33), BMI 1.004 (p=0.26, age terms unchanged when added).

## Submitted hypothesis (in output/HYPOTHESIS.md and hypothesis.json)
Weak, non-robust, descriptive-only age association: negative and marginally curvilinear as delivered (~−0.9 pp/yr at age 28; −6.8 pp from 24 to 32; corr −0.041), flat and indistinguishable from zero once curator-filled rows are removed (corr +0.016), no U-shape or in-support turning point; best read as a near-flat life-cycle savings profile plus a differential-missingness artifact concentrated at older ages and a shift toward net saving rather than reduced withdrawing — income, not age, dominates. Mechanism verdict: the shape favors "flat life-cycle profile + missingness artifact" over a strong time-preference gradient.

## Limitations
Mean-fill detection is inferential (exact float matches on column means, plus an all-default fill signature in 1,462 rows), not documented in any codebook; clean-subset exclusion is complete-case and could itself be MNAR-biased; age spans only 9 years so any curvature is weakly identified; the 1,057.448 top-code (167 rows) is retained unsmoothed as instructed and may still distort the as-delivered income coefficient; INCOME units assumed $thousands; 1989 cross-section, so age/period/cohort are inseparable and nothing here is causal.

payload.hypothesis: In this NLSY79 1989 cross-section (n=12,686, P(DISSAVED=1)=23.6%), age is only weakly related to dissaving, and the small negative gradient the delivered file shows is an artifact of the curator's mean-imputation rather than a behavioral relationship. As delivered, older respondents are less likely to dissave: adjusted logistic OR=0.955 per year of age (95% CI 0.938-0.973, p=6.5e-07), predicted P(DISSAVED) falling from 0.253 at age 24 to 0.185 at age 32 (-6.8 percentage points), corr(AGE,DISSAVED)=-0.041. The quadratic age term is barely significant (AGE_c^2=-0.0089, p=0.042; LR vs linear chi2=4.76, df=1, p=0.029), saturated age dummies add nothing (chi2=7.52, df=6, p=0.275), and the implied maximum at age 25.5 has a bootstrap 95% CI of 18.6-26.8, i.e. largely below the observed 24-32 support, so the shape is a mild monotone decline rather than a U or inverted-U. The gradient is not robust: 4,256 rows (33.6%) carry the mean-fill signature (INCOME exactly 47.279064 in 3,963 rows; BMI exactly 25.158946 in 2,493 rows), the fill share rises monotonically with age (26-29% at ages 24-27 to 41-47% at ages 30-32) and filled rows dissave far less often (11.9% vs 29.2%). Excluding them (n=8,430) the age effect vanishes: AGE_c=-0.0012 (p=0.91), AGE_c^2=-0.0029 (p=0.56), joint age LR p=0.84, OR/yr=1.000 (0.979-1.021), predicted probability flat at 0.289-0.297, corr flipping to +0.016. Tested inside the full sample the slope differs sharply by fill status (LR interaction chi2=38.65, df=1, p=5e-10): slope -0.0004 (p=0.97) among non-filled rows, additional -0.151 (p<1e-10) inside filled rows; dropping only the 2,151 exact duplicate rows, which are themselves the fill artifact, also erases the gradient (AGE_c=+0.0055, p=0.58). Composition rather than withdrawing drives what remains: separating dissave / unchanged-or-no-savings / saved-more, the as-delivered gradient loads entirely on saved-more vs unchanged (+0.112/yr, p<1e-16) and is absent from dissave vs unchanged (+0.0095, p=0.39), with both contrasts null in the clean subset. Income is the dominant correlate: in the clean subset log(1+INCOME) gives OR=1.365 per log-dollar (95% CI 1.295-1.440, p<1e-29), raising predicted dissaving 12.3 points from the 10th to the 90th income percentile versus -0.2 points for the whole 24-to-32 age span; Black OR=1.36, male OR=0.91, Hispanic and BMI null. Conclusion: age has a weak, non-robust, descriptively-only association with dissaving over the narrow 24-32 window - negative and marginally curvilinear as delivered (about -0.9 percentage points per year at age 28), flat and statistically indistinguishable from zero once mean-imputed rows are removed, with no U-shape or in-range turning point. It is best read as a near-flat life-cycle savings profile plus a differential-missingness artifact concentrated at older ages, and as a shift toward net saving rather than reduced withdrawing, not as evidence for an age-graded time-preference gradient.
payload.workflow: Inspection (shape/completeness/duplicate and mean-fill detection) -> constructed was_imputed fill flag, MALE, log1p(INCOME)+INCOME==0, INCOME quartiles, AGE_c=AGE-28 and AGE_c^2, 3-level savings outcome -> descriptive tables of dissaving rate by exact age and age group with Wilson CIs for full/clean/dedup/filled-only samples plus fill share by age and by outcome -> adjusted logistic regressions (GLM binomial) on the as-delivered file (primary, no dedup), clean non-imputed subset (co-primary) and dedup sensitivity, each with linear, quadratic and saturated-age specifications, LR tests for quadratic vs linear and saturated vs quadratic, bootstrap (B=400, seed 20261025) CIs for the turning point, age-specific marginal effects with delta-method CIs, and predicted-probability spans for age (24 vs 32) and income (p10 vs p90) -> was_imputed indicator model and age x was_imputed interaction LR tests inside the full sample to localize the gradient by fill status -> multinomial logit (dissave / same / saved more) sensitivity on both samples -> covariate checks (income quartiles, top-code retained unsmoothed, BMI added last) -> consolidated tables in output/SUMMARY.md and output/results.json, hypothesis text in output/HYPOTHESIS.md.
